text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Twenty-seven people including 17 policemen are killed by armed raiders as fighting between security officers and bandits intensifies in Marsabit district in northeastern Kenya.
- President Daniel arap Moi dismisses as a forgery a letter purportedly written by him exonerating business tycoon Ketan Somaia from dubious business dealings.
- A primary schoolteacher denies in court that she poisoned a soda which an assistant minister took moments before he died at a public function.
- Opposition leaders reiterate calls for a constitutional conference.
- More than 11 million Kenyans or 43 percent of the population are poor while another two million are unemployed, a government official says.
- The Kenya Union of Commercial Food and Allied Workers calls off national bank strike.
- Two more suspects are charged in a Nairobi court with the theft of 96 million shillings from Standard Chartered bank.
- The government hits out at oil companies for failing to reduce the price of liquefied petroleum gas following a drop in world prices for crude.
- A court discharges three primary school teachers charged with murdering a pupil, citing a lack of evidence. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
